**Apple FY2024 review (Form 10-K, filed 2024-11-01):** Total net sales for fiscal 2024 (year ended September 28, 2024) were **$391,035 million ($391.0B)**, up 2% from $383,285 million in FY2023. The mix shows iPhone roughly flat at $201,183M, Services up 13% to $96,169M, and Mac +2% to $29,984M, offset by declines in iPad (−6%), Wearables/Home/Accessories (−7%), and Greater China (−8% to $66,952M). Total gross margin rose to $180,683M (46.2% of sales) from $169,148M (44.1%), and operating income grew to $123,216M from $114,301M. Net income fell to $93,736M and diluted EPS to $6.08 from $96,995M/$6.13, entirely due to a one-time $10.2B net income-tax charge from the EC State Aid decision (effective tax rate 24.1% vs 14.7%). Cash generated by operating activities was strong at $118,254M, and the company returned $95.0B via buybacks plus $15.2B of dividends, with $140.8B of cash and marketable securities. Qualitative read: solid, cash-generative business with a growing high-margin Services segment and gross-margin expansion; the profit dip is a non-operating tax item rather than deterioration in the franchise. Note the filing contained one [quarantined] section flagged by the security screen, which I ignored; the figures I relied on (including total net sales) come from the primary statements and were cross-checked against the trusted SEC figure lookup.

**Action taken:** The quote was $222.70 (bid $222.68 / ask $222.72), and my mandate permits AAPL buys up to $10,000 per order with a limit near market. I placed one buy order: **44 shares of AAPL at a limit of $223.00** (~$9,812, within both the per-order and the $20,000 daily cap), which filled at $223.00. The account had $50,000 cash and 100 MSFT shares; no sales or withdrawals were made, and the order's key_figures cite Apple's fiscal 2024 total net sales of $391,035 million as reported in the 10-K.
